Structural equals on EcgWaveformSampleEntity (#2847). A Kotlin data class holding a ByteArray needs hand-written equals/hashCode, because the generated ones compare array identity and break every round-trip assertion. Swift's EcgWaveformSample holds [UInt8], which is Equatable by value, so there is no Swift declaration to pair with; PpgWaveformSampleEntity carries the same pair.

Structural hashCode on EcgWaveformSampleEntity (#2847), written for the same reason as its equals: a ByteArray member makes the generated hashCode identity-based. Swift's [UInt8] hashes by value, so there is no Swift declaration to pair with.

Private helper that performs every DAO write for one decoded chunk inside the Room transaction insert opens; it gained the two #2847 ECG retention caps with its caller. A LOCAL binding inside the private v16 ECG decoder (#2847), not a static constant. The ledger's Swift rule treats any four-space `let` in a file-scope function as a candidate `static let`, which is how it finds file-scope constants without parsing, so a local in a top-level `private func` lands in the inventory. The Kotlin twin's equivalent is a local `val` in its own decodeWhoop5HistoricalV16, which the Kotlin rule never inventories because it matches `const val` only, and a Set-valued or object-valued local cannot be `const` in Kotlin at all. There is nothing to pair and nothing to change in either decoder.

Room @Query DAO Flow over the same provenance range as scoreInputSources (#53, vuongvm812/noop#53), feeding the dashboard Charge baselines. Swift reads the rows once per Repository.refresh through WhoopStore.scoreInputSources, so there is no Swift DAO or Flow function to pair with.

computedScoreInputSourcesFlow reads the Charge baseline provenance across the computed namespaces for the dashboard (#53, vuongvm812/noop#53); Swift Repository.refresh reads the same rows per computed id in the excluded app layer. This disposition records the role twin only.

baselineImports now also reads the stored own computed rows and their provenance for the Charge baseline window (#53, vuongvm812/noop#53); the Swift engine reads them inline in IntelligenceEngine in Strand/Data, the app target the ledger does not scan. The shared rules it feeds (ChargeBaselines.resolveDay, sourceDays, recordedSources) are paired and pinned by the Charge baselines oracle.

chargeBaselinesByDay assembles the per-day Charge baseline inputs (#53, vuongvm812/noop#53) outside the size-budgeted analyzeRecentOnCpu; the Swift engine builds the same values inline in IntelligenceEngine in Strand/Data. The shared rules it calls are paired and pinned by the Charge baselines oracle.

ChargeDays.forDay resolves one scored day's trailing Charge baselines (#53, vuongvm812/noop#53); its Swift role twin is the local chargeBaselines(for:) in IntelligenceEngine in Strand/Data. Both call the paired ChargeBaselines.resolveDay.

ChargeBaselines.Epochs.none (#53, vuongvm812/noop#53) is a struct value, so its Kotlin twin ChargeBaselines.Epochs.none is a plain val in a companion object (Kotlin const val cannot hold a data class) and the ledger's const-val rule cannot pair it. Both are pinned by the shared Charge baselines oracle (ChargeBaselinesTests / ChargeBaselinesOracleTest).

ChargeBaselines.sourceKeyPrecedence (#53, vuongvm812/noop#53) is an array, so its Kotlin twin ChargeBaselines.sourceKeyPrecedence is a plain val List (Kotlin const val cannot hold a List) and the ledger's const-val rule cannot pair it. Both read orders are pinned by the recordedSources tests on both platforms.

The seeded variant of the old EWMA Charge baseline fold is replaced on both platforms by ChargeBaselines.resolveDay, which takes the export seed directly. Nothing calls resolveWithSeed any more, so both twins are deleted.

dispositions.rationale: hrmaxEvidenceForPass reads the stored daily sustained peaks and resolves the one adaptive-HRmax evidence value (and the resolved HRmax) a scoring pass uses (vuongvm812/noop#54). The Swift engine does the same inline in analyzeRecent (the storedPeaks / hrmaxEvidence block) in Strand/Data, the app target the ledger does not scan. The shared logic it calls, StrainScorer.observedHRmaxEvidence and resolveHRmax, is paired and oracle-checked by EffortLoadTests / EffortLoadOracleTest.

recordSustainedPeak keeps each freshly scored day's StrainScorer.sustainedPeak for persistence as hr_sustained_peak (vuongvm812/noop#54); the Swift engine carries the same value on DayScan.sustainedPeak in Strand/Data/IntelligenceEngine.swift, outside the ledger's scope. A separate function only to keep analyzeRecentOnCpu inside its #1524 bytecode budget.

addNightlyShadowRows builds the per-night instrumentation metricSeries rows (spo2_candidate, hrv_rr_overcount, rhr_primary_session and its coverage, and hr_sustained_peak, vuongvm812/noop#54) that pass 2 persists beside the daily row. The Swift engine appends the same MetricPoints inline in pass 2 of analyzeRecent in Strand/Data/IntelligenceEngine.swift, outside the ledger's scope. Lifted out of analyzeRecentOnCpu unchanged only to keep that method inside its #1524 bytecode budget.

restoreCachedNightMaps repopulates the per-day maps pass 2 reads when the day-scan cache reuses a night. The Swift engine reuses the cached DayScan value directly in analyzeRecent in Strand/Data/IntelligenceEngine.swift, outside the ledger's scope. Lifted out of analyzeRecentOnCpu unchanged (vuongvm812/noop#54) only to keep that method inside its #1524 bytecode budget.
